items.title: Pinching-Antenna Systems (PASS): A Tutorial
items.abstract: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) present a break-through among the flexible-antenna technologies, and distinguish themselves by facilitating large-scale antenna reconfiguration, line-of-sight creation, scalable implementation, and near-field benefits, thus bringing wireless communications from the “last mile” to the “last meter”. To illustrate the benefits of PASS in next-generation wireless networks, a comprehensive tutorial is presented in this paper. First, the fundamentals of PASS are discussed, including PASS signal models, hardware models, power radiation models, and pinching antenna (PA) activation methods. Building upon this, the information-theoretic capacity limits achieved by PASS are characterized, and several typical performance metrics of PASS-based communications are analyzed to demonstrate its superiority over conventional antenna technologies. Next, the pinching beamforming design is investigated. The corresponding power scaling law is first characterized for the single-waveguide single-user case. For the joint transmit and pinching design in the general multiple-waveguide case, 1) a pair of transmission strategies is proposed for PASS-based single-user communications to validate the superiority of PASS, namely sub-connected and fully connected structures in terms of the connections between the baseband radio frequency chains and waveguides; and 2) three practical protocols are proposed for facilitating PASS-based multi-user communications, namely waveguide switching, waveguide division, and waveguide multiplexing. A possible implementation of PASS in wideband communications is further highlighted. Moreover, the channel state information (CSI) acquisition in PASS is elaborated with a pair of promising solutions, based on pilot-based channel estimation and beam training, respectively. To overcome the high complexity and suboptimality inherent in conventional convex-optimization-based approaches, machine-learning-based methods for operating PASS are also explored, focusing on selected deep neural network architectures and training algorithms. Finally, several promising applications of PASS in next-generation wire-less networks are highlighted to motivate future works.

On higher-order quantum corrections to the photon polarization tensor in the Schwinger model
items.abstract: In this paper, we examine the theory of quantum electrodynamics with massless fermions in two dimensions (the Schwinger model). First, we derive the effective action of the photon by integrating out the fermionic degrees of freedom. Then, using this effective action and the scattering-matrix approach, we prove that the amplitudes of all diagrams contributing to the photon polarization tensor at two- and three-loop levels vanish. Next, we demonstrate that all other quantum corrections arising from higher-order perturbations also vanish. We therefore conclude, within perturbation theory, that the photon polarization tensor, and consequently the Schwinger mass, are one-loop exact.

items.title: Novel temperature-insensitive Fe-based medium-entropy alloys with extraordinary strength-ductility synergy from 77 K to 973 K
items.abstract: Developing an alloy with mechanical stability across a wide temperature range, excellent mechanical properties and low cost has great engineering significance, but achieving this synergy in a single alloy remains highly challenging. This study proposes an innovative design method for advanced medium-entropy alloys (MEAs), and successfully synthesizes a low-cost (Fe44Ni30Cr15Al7Ti2Si2)99.6Zr0.1B0.1C0.2 MEA. This MEA has exceptionally temperature-insensitive mechanical properties between 77 K and 973 K, retaining high yield strength (~760 MPa at 298 K, ~870 MPa at 77 K, ~620 MPa at 973 K) and ductility over 25% at all tested temperatures. This performance exceeds almost all reported alloys, including those with high Co/Ni content, enabled by the synergy of nanoscale L12 precipitates, short-range order, dislocations, slip bands, stacking faults and twin boundaries. This highlights the potential of Fe-based MEAs for key applications in aerospace, automotive and energy sectors, meeting the performance requirements of modern industries under dynamic environment conditions.

items.title: Multi-Modal Foundation Models for Space-Air-Ground Integrated 6G and Beyond Networks: A Survey and Tutorial
items.venue: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society
items.abstract: Space-air-ground integrated networks (SAGINs) are emerging as a key architectural paradigm for 6G and beyond wireless systems, enabling seamless connectivity by integrating terrestrial radio access networks with aerial platforms and non-terrestrial networks (NTNs). The operation of SAGINs, however, departs significantly from conventional terrestrial assumptions due to high mobility, Doppler dynamics, intermittent connectivity, long and variable round-trip times, gateway bottlenecks, and strong cross-layer coupling. These characteristics motivate intelligence frameworks that leverage heterogeneous contextual information beyond traditional radio frequency (RF) measurements. This paper presents a comprehensive survey and tutorial on multi-modal foundation models (FMs) for SAGIN-centric 6G systems. The survey first introduces a structured taxonomy of SAGIN data modalities, including RF/channel state information (CSI), topology graphs, trajectories and ephemeris, telemetry and traffic traces, weather and atmospheric context, and sensing signals enabled by integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). It then reviews representation and tokenization strategies for heterogeneous wireless modalities and surveys emerging architecture families for multi-modal FMs, including early, late, and hybrid fusion designs, cross-attention mechanisms, mixture-of-experts models, hierarchical multi-timescale architectures, and retrieval-augmented frameworks. The paper further summarizes training paradigms such as masked modeling, cross-modal contrastive learning, and predictive pretraining, together with adaptation strategies including parameter-efficient fine-tuning, continual learning, and federated updates. In addition, the survey discusses system-level considerations for integrating multi-modal FMs into network control loops and deployment environments, covering distributed inference, model compression, intermittency-aware operation, and safety constraints. Finally, the paper outlines benchmarking principles for evaluating multi-modal intelligence in SAGINs and identifies key open research challenges and future directions for building robust, deployable AI-native 6G networks.

items.title: Lower Temperature–Accelerated Degradation of Large-Format High-Ni NMC Pouch Cells Associated with Cathode Oxygen Loss
items.abstract: Temperature-dependent degradation of Ni-rich lithium-ion batteries is commonly attributed to high-temperature cathode degradation or low-temperature lithium plating. However, behavior at moderate temperatures in commercial-format cells remains poorly understood because most previous studies have focused on temperature extremes or small-format cells. Herein, 58.3-Ah commercial Ni-rich NMC811/graphite pouch cells were cycled using a 2C–1.5C–1C multistage fast-charging protocol with a full-cell cutoff voltage of 4.15 V at average cell temperatures of 20°C, 29°C, 37°C, and 41°C. Capacity fading accelerated as temperature decreased despite the smaller accessible depth of discharge at lower temperature.,Electrochemical analysis indicated that the severe degradation was associated with increased loss of lithium inventory, loss of negative-electrode active material, and Li-ion transport resistance. Post-mortem microscopy and depth-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) revealed a dense, oxygen-rich inorganic interphase on the anode cycled at 20°C, without persistent morphological evidence of lithium plating or transition metal crossover. On the cathode, X-ray diffraction with Rietveld refinement and O 1s XPS revealed pronounced lattice distortion, structural disorder, and strong oxygen-loss signatures at lower temperatures, without increased bulk Li/Ni cation mixing or a corresponding increase in the Ni²⁺-associated satellite contribution. Li-transport limitations and increased polarization at lower temperatures are therefore proposed to amplify reaction and Li-concentration heterogeneity across the electrode thickness and within individual secondary particles. Local Li-deficient regions may promote TM–O destabilization and oxygen-loss-associated reactions, accelerating electrolyte and LiPF₆ decomposition and the growth of an O-, F-, and P-rich inorganic interphase on the anode.

items.title: Long‐Term Deflection of Chloride-Exposed RRAC Beams under,Wetting–Drying Cycles and Sustained Load: Tests and Analysis
items.abstract: Recycled aggregate concrete (RAC) offers a sustainable solution for construction waste utilization; however, the long-term deflection behavior of reinforced RAC (RRAC) beams under combined chloride attack, wetting-drying cycles, and sustained loading remains unclear, and current design codes lack reliable prediction methods. This paper reports selected findings from a comprehensive experimental investigation into the long-term deflection response of 24 RRAC beam specimens subjected to varying recycled coarse aggregate (RCA) replacement ratios (50% and 100%), sustained mechanical load levels (0.3, 0.5, and 0.7), and chloride-induced corrosion rates. Corrosion was accelerated through cyclic wetting-drying exposure in a saline environment maintained at a constant elevated temperature of , while sustained loads were maintained throughout the 360-day test period. A simplified method for predicting the long-term deflection of RRAC beams is developed based on a time-dependent constitutive model following the Chinese code JTG 3362-2018. The proposed method accounts for ambient temperature and humidity, chloride-induced corrosion, cracking, tension stiffening, nonlinear creep, and shrinkage, and is validated against experimental data. The results indicate that an increase in any of the three factors—RCA replacement ratio, load level, or wetting–drying cycle duration—significantly accelerates both corrosion development and deflection growth. Under identical conditions, beams with 100% RCA replacement exhibit larger deflections than those with 50% RCA, and this discrepancy widens over time. Validation yields a mean measured-to-predicted deflection ratio of 0.87 (COV = 11.63%) at a load level of 0.3, and approximately 1.00 (COV < 4.50%) for load levels exceeding 0.3. Shrinkage contributes about 13% to the total deflection. The proposed method is simple, reliable, and applicable to structural design and service-life assessment.

items.title: Load-Pull-Driven Current Ratio Optimization for Accurate Load Modulation of Asymmetric Doherty Power Amplifiers
items.abstract: Conventional Doherty power amplifiers (DPAs) often suffer from performance degradation due to inaccurate load modulation, primarily caused by relying on idealized fixed current ratio and neglecting the intricate nonlinearities of practical transistors. This paper proposes a generalized and systematic design methodology for asymmetric DPAs (ADPAs) based on load-pull-driven current ratio ( $\delta$ ) optimization. By identifying a specific $\delta$ that satisfies the carrier amplifier's optimal impedance conditions at both saturation and output power back-off (OBO), the proposed method establishes the desired load modulation trajectory linking the OBO and saturation impedance conditions. The proposed design methodology effectively bridges the gap between active device characterization and matching network synthesis by deriving $\delta$ directly from load-pull data. To verify the proposed approach, two ADPA prototypes targeting 6-dB and 9-dB OBO were designed and fabricated at 2.45 GHz. The 6-dB prototype achieves a measured saturated output power of 45 dBm with a peak drain efficiency of 72.3~\%, while maintaining 68.5~\% drain efficiency at 6-dB OBO. The 9-dB prototype achieves 43.82~dBm output power with 71.87~\% drain efficiency at saturation and 73.75~\% drain efficiency at 9-dB OBO. These results demonstrate that the proposed design methodology provides an effective and scalable design solution for high-performance ADPAs.

items.title: Lightweight Sensor Fusion for Autonomous Driving: A Systematic Review and Deployment-Oriented Evidence Synthesis
items.abstract: The deployment bottleneck of autonomous driving perception has shifted from detection accuracy alone to deterministic computational constraints on automotive edge systems. Although recent multi-sensor fusion methods achieve strong benchmark performance, their computational cost and inference latency remain difficult to reconcile with real-time execution on production-grade systems-on-chip (SoCs). This paper presents a deployment-oriented systematic review that frames lightweight sensor fusion as a constrained design problem: reducing latency L, memory footprint M, and energy consumption E while maintaining accuracy A ≥ Amin, inference time T ≤ Tdeadline, and power consumption P ≤ Pbudget. Following the PRISMA protocol, we analyze 59 retained studies and propose a three-dimensional taxonomy spanning fusion level, spatial alignment paradigm, and lightweight optimization. We then synthesize 11 representative algorithms through deployment-oriented evidence fields covering accuracy, reported computational complexity, latency-derived FPS, hardware context, and source category. The review identifies and analyzes four trade-offs thatgovern the deployment envelope, including accuracy–efficiency scaling, modal-ity complementarity, calibration robustness, and safety-performance tension. items.title: Inverse design of polarization-insensitive full-color waveguide combiner’s in-coupling grating
items.abstract: We report an inverse-design framework to mitigate the re-coupling loss in unpolarized, full-color augmented reality (AR) waveguide combiners. By incorporating the coupling count distribution into the optimization loop and partitioning the grating into zones with tailored heights, the framework effectively suppresses re-coupling loss in finite apertures. A hybrid optimization algorithm yields a polarization-insensitive, single-layer metagrating with a shared freeform metagrating and varying heights optimized across different zones, balancing in-coupling efficiency and internal reflectivity per region. Numerical demonstrations show an average efficiency of 30% across RGB channels over a 20° FOV, with improved angular uniformity and color balance over conventional designs. Fabrication robustness analysis confirms the device maintains high efficiency even with height errors up to ±20 nm. By intrinsically achieving polarization-insensitive diffraction, our design obviates the need for polarization conversion elements, offering inherent compatibility with unpolarized sources and providing a robust and scalable solution for high-brightness AR displays.

items.title: Integrating magnetic resonance coupling with radio frequency energy to wirelessly charge mobile device batteries
items.abstract: Mobile devices are rapidly evolving, with new features being continuously integrated into smartphones and an increasing number of apps being developed to enhance user convenience. The convenience of these mobile devices is constrained only by the lifespan of their batteries. The reliance on mobile devices like smartphones necessitates frequent battery charging, which can be inconvenient for users since the device becomes unusable during charging. Additionally, unnecessary charging leads to wasted electricity, a significant concern given the ongoing electricity crisis. Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) offers an efficient solution for charging mobile device batteries without the need for wires. This research aimed to present the results of a WPT prototype circuit that combines magnetic resonance coupling with harvested Radio Frequency (RF) energy to enable wireless power transmission for recharging mobile devices. Initial work on the RF energy harvesting circuit has been conducted, yielding promising results. WPT enables the transmission of energy or power from a transmitting component to a receiving component through a pulsating magnetic field. This process enables electricity to travel wirelessly from a power source, such as harvested RF energy, to an electrical load, like a mobile device battery, without the need for physical connectors, bridging the gap through non-contact transmission. A wireless power system fundamentally relies on a pair of coils: one for transmitting energy and the other for receiving it. The transmitting coil is energized by an alternating current (AC), generating a magnetic field that induces a current in the receiving coil. Harvested RF energy is converted into high-frequency AC through precisely designed electronics embedded within the transmitter. The AC is supplied to a copper wire coil in the transmitter, generating a magnetic field. When the receiving coil is placed near the magnetic field, it induces an alternating current (AC) within the coil. The integrated electronic components in the receiving device then convert the AC into direct current (DC), delivering useful power. The experimental design of the WPT charging circuit, incorporating an RF harvesting circuit and magnetic resonance coupling, has shown promising performance. A mathematical modelling and simulation research approach was employed to integrate magnetic resonance coupling with harvested RF energy in the wireless charging system. The developed model included constructing a WPT charging circuit prototype that incorporated RF-harvested energy and magnetic resonance coupling (magnetic coils). The LTSpice simulation software was utilised to evaluate the feasibility of integrating capacitors into the circuit layout. The study's findings validate the successful development of a WPT charging circuit capable of wirelessly charging a mobile device battery. Furthermore, the research explores an alternative energy storage solution by substituting a capacitor for the mobile device battery.

items.title: Integrated Multiport High-Gain Modified Zeta Bidirectional DC-DCConverter with Coupled Inductor and ISO-Based PV MPPT control⋆
items.abstract: The increasing demand for eco-friendly transportation solutions necessitates the implementation ofefficient power converter technology in future transportation infrastructure. This paper presents amethod for integrating multiple energy sources with integrated converters for electric vehicles. Theproposed approach suggests integrating a two-switch buck-boost converter with a coupled inductorbased modified zeta bidirectional DC-DC converter (BDC) to achieve medium and high voltagegain configurations. Mathematical analyses of the proposed topology are conducted in continuousconduction mode (CCM) and discontinuous conduction mode (DCM). The proposed model usesImproved Snake Optimizer (ISO) optimization to achieve Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT),resulting in rapid and stable power tracking. Model order reduction and Type III compensation areemployed to achieve closed-loop control performance for the BDC. The proposed topology parameteroptimization is examined using MATLAB/Simulink, while the simulation of BLDC motor load isperformed on PLECS. The experimental results for the proposed design show that the integratedconverter can achieve a voltage gain of 120V while maintaining a low current ripple during forwardmode operation. The converter achieves 93.5% efficiency at a load of 237W, and on-board testing withthe proposed bidirectional converter demonstrates a 15-20% increase in driving range.

Hollow-Core Fiber in Direct-Detection Optical Networks: Technology Readiness, Deployment Drivers, and Adoption Outlook
items.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of hollow-core fiber (HCF) for intensity-modulation and direct-detection (IMDD) optical networks, covering fiber-level physics, system-level performance, and deployment economics. We quantify the three principal advantages of anti-resonant HCF over standard single-mode fiber (SMF) for IMDD: (i) chromatic dispersion of 2-4 ps/(nm km) versus 17 ps/(nm km), which shifts the first dispersion-induced power-fading null from about 10 GHz to 20-28 GHz at 40 km, extending the dispersion-limited reach by 4-8x; (ii) a nonlinear coefficient approximately 1,000x lower than silica, permitting launch powers of +10 to +20 dBm and yielding 7-17 dB of additional link budget; and (iii) a group index near unity (ng about 1.003), reducing propagation latency by 31%. We further analyze inter-modal interference (IMI) as the dominant impairment for HCF-based IMDD. We show that differential modal attenuation (DMA) exceeding 12 dB/km suppresses IMI-induced crosstalk below the -30 dB multipath interference threshold required for PAM4. The reduced dispersion also lowers the required feed-forward equalizer (FFE) tap count by 3-6x, directly decreasing noise enhancement penalty and DSP complexity. A deployment cost model across five application scenarios - intra-data center, campus DCI, metro DCI, 5G fronthaul, and PON - reveals that fiber cable constitutes only 5-10% of outside-plant deployment cost, and that coherent transceiver avoidance savings of $1000 to $2000 per transceiver can offset the current HCF premium at metro distances. We provide a technology adoption roadmap indicating that HCF is economically justified now for intra-DC and campus DCI, with metro DCI following in 2027-2030 as manufacturing costs continue to decline.

Hidden Coupling: Rethinking Commodity Diversification with Mutual Information
items.abstract: Abstract The case for commodity diversification is usually argued from linear correlation, yet allocation decisions can be questioned precisely when correlation misses nonlinear co-movement. This paper asks: do commodities truly diversify equities when it matters, and can we size exposure accordingly? Using daily ETFs from 2020–2025, I compare absolute Pearson correlation with mutual information (MI) and benchmark observed MI against its Gaussian-implied value at the prevailing correlation. Two results stand out. In calm or trending markets, both commodity-laden and non-commodity mixes explain very little of SPY’s uncertainty: correlation overstates the practical distinctiveness of commodities. In systemic stress (e.g., 2020), portfolios can exhibit low correlation yet sharply elevated MI, revealing hidden, nonlinear coupling consistent with financialization, even as commodity sleeves deliver right-tail payoffs. I then operationalize MI in a sizing overlay that caps the commodity sleeve when market-scaled MI exceeds its Gaussian benchmark. In out-of-sample tests (2020–2024), the MI rule delivers very small, directionally favorable reductions in expected shortfall and drawdown relative to an identically constrained correlation trigger, but with materially lower turnover. MI is thus a practical complement to correlation, useful for detecting regime shifts and sizing commodity exposure when dependence intensifies near the left tail.

Half-Metallic Ferrimagnetism and High Spin Polarization in Ba2GdMnO6: A Density Functional Theory Study
items.abstract: The structural, mechanical, electronic, magnetic, optical, and thermoelectric properties of the ferrimagnetic double perovskite Ba2GdMnO6 were investigated using density functional theory. Thermodynamic, dynamic, and mechanical stability are confirmed by negative formation energy, absence of imaginary phonon modes, and Born criteria. Ferrimagnetic ordering is the ground state, from antiparallel Gd (+6.82 μB) and Mn (-1.95 μB) moments, giving a net moment of 9.93 μB. High stiffness (B = 163.26 GPa, E = 229.31 GPa, G=90.57 GPa) accompanies ductile behavior, confirmed by Pugh’s ratio, Poisson’s ratio, Cauchy Pressure, and Kleinman’s parameter. It shows near half-metallicity, with a semiconducting spin-up channel (~1.10 eV gap) and metallic spin-down channel, yielding 97% spin polarization. Very strong optical absorption (>106 cm-1) spans the higher-energy UV region, and thermoelectric analysis yields an electronic ZT of 3.37 at 800 K. These results establish Ba2GdMnO6 as a promising spintronic, optoelectronic, and thermoelectric material.

items.title: Grid-Forming Control With DC-Link Compensation for Modular Multifunctional Fast Charging Stations
Glow Plug Integrated Solar Heater for Reducing Initial Waiting Period of Evaporation Lag and Improve Thermal Efficiency in Solar Still Desalination
items.abstract: The current solar desalination process is facing a challenge of longer time for the brine temperature to reach the evaporation threshold during the winter with cooler ambient temperature, cloudy, and the initial hours of the day. This study aims to address the challenge by reducing initial waiting period of evaporation lag through integrating a glow plug enabled solar powered water heater (SPWH), operates at low resistance (0.48 – 0.81 Ω) and high power (12 V, 25 A, 300 W). Prior to implementation, mathematical modelling is employed to determine the appropriate sizing of the PV system, battery, cable, and maximum power point tracking (MPPT) controller. The results demonstrate a significant increase in the temperature of the brine, reaching 79.2°C within 45 minutes at a rate of 0.96°C/min. The temperature profile demonstrates that the brine water, reaching a steady peak with minimal fluctuations of ± 2°C, retains heat more effectively than the chamber temperature due to its higher specific heat capacity. Throughout the experiment, the average brine temperature is maintained at 70.58°C, even on a day with heavy cloud cover (average irradiance 418 W/m2). Another noteworthy finding is that the system can produce more than 3.35 kg/m2of freshwater per day with the highest thermal efficiency of 68.18% under cloudy ambient conditions. The electrical performance of the system proves to be highly stable, with the voltages of both the PV system and battery experiencing minimal fluctuations not more than 0.9%. In addition, the system has achieved a cost-effective production rate of $0.09/kg. By employing this technique, challenges related to limited access to clean drinking water, scarcity of freshwater sources, and water quality issues in remote Malaysian islands can be effectively overcome.

items.title: Gasification reactivity of unburned char from high-volatile bituminous coals injection in blast furnace: Coupling of parent coal properties, char microstructure and ash
items.abstract: Excessive accumulation of unburned char (UBC) in the blast furnace can impair permeability and constrain further increases in the pulverized-coal injection (PCI) rate unless UBC is effectively consumed, primarily through subsequent gasification. Nine high-volatile bituminous coals with comparable properties were rapidly combusted in a drop tube furnace to produce UBCs with different burnout levels. Their thermal conversion and CO2 gasification behaviors were investigated using simultaneous thermal analysis, complemented by pore-structure, microcrystalline, and mineralogical characterization. UBC gasification reactivity showed no direct correlation with parent-coal burnout but remained strongly related to parent-coal reactivity at burnout levels below 80% (R2 > 0.92). Increasing burnout decreased both the specific surface area and aromatic interlayer spacing d002; however, neither parameter showed a consistently positive correlation with UBC gasification reactivity. Instead, Ca-bearing minerals in the UBC ash promoted gasification through low-temperature carbonation followed by high-temperature carbonate decomposition, thereby generating or regenerating catalytically active CaO, while carbonate decomposition may also contribute to local pore development. The associated mass-gain and decomposition features in the TG-DTG-DTA curves reflected the catalytic contribution of discrete Ca-bearing species. As burnout increased, mineral catalysis progressively outweighed the adverse effects of pore deterioration and increasing carbon structural order, ultimately becoming a dominant factor governing UBC gasification reactivity. These findings reveal the coupled effects of parent-coal properties, UBC microstructure, and ash-mineral transformations on the thermal conversion and CO2 gasification reactivity of UBC.

items.title: Exact Semiclassical Dynamics in a Multidimensional Quartic Potential: Multi-Flavor Instantons and Pre-Factor Dominance at Strong Coupling
items.abstract: We present an exact semi-classical analysis of a coupled multi-degree-of-freedom quantum system governed by a symmetric quartic potential with four degenerate minima. Starting from the Euclidean path integral, we identify distinct paths—longitudinal, transverse, and diagonal—corresponding to distinct instanton configurations that mediate tunneling between vacua. The continuous translational zero mode for each coupled trajectory is extracted rigorously by transforming the fluctuation operator into a comoving rotating frame, explicitly incorporating curvature-induced fictitious forces. By evaluating the exact functional determinants via the Gelfand-Yaglom method and mapping the multi-flavor dilute instanton gas onto a weighted $K_4$ adjacency matrix, we analytically derive the transition amplitudes and ground-state energy splittings. Crucially, our exact continuum treatment reveals that for strong coupling, the usual exponential can be overpowered in certain parameter ranges by the "pre-factor". This quantity, which arises from quadratic level fluctuations in the direction transverse to the free direction, turns out to have an essential singularity that would be hard to spot in standard discretized instanton approximations.

items.title: Engineered Dissonance - How Digital Design Shapes Empathy, Polarization, and the Capacity for Social Cooperation
items.abstract: Contemporary democratic societies face a convergent crisis: declining empathy, intensifying polarization, and a diminishing capacity to cooperate across social and ideological lines. Existing scholarship has examined this crisis largely through a content-centric lens, focusing on disinformation, partisan media, and echo chambers, while paying comparatively little attention to the role of digital platform architecture itself. This paper argues that the design features of digital platforms, including infinite scroll, autoplay, variable-reward notification systems, and engagement-optimized recommender algorithms, function as an active environmental force shaping cognition and emotion, independent of the specific content they deliver. Drawing on an interdisciplinary synthesis of psychology, neuroscience, communication research, and political science, the paper traces a mechanistic pathway from platform architecture through behavioural reinforcement and attentional capture to reduced reflective processing, diminished perspective-taking, eroded empathic capacity, algorithmic amplification of moral-emotional content, affective polarization, and ultimately reduced social cooperation. The paper integrates evidence on dopaminergic reward conditioning, default mode network suppression, desensitization, and the stripping of social cues in digitally mediated interaction to propose a unified conceptual model linking design to democratic dysfunction. It concludes by considering the implications of this model for platform governance, design ethics, and future regulatory approaches to digital architecture.

Effect of silane coupling agent grafting coverage on water transport in C–S–H nanochannels: Experimental investigation and molecular dynamics simulation​
items.abstract: Silane coupling agent (SCA) can effectively reduce the water absorption of recycled concrete powder/ground granulated blast-furnace slag (RCP/GGBS)-based artificial aggregates (AAs), but the regulatory mechanism of KH570 grafting coverage on water transport within calcium silicate hydrate (C–S–H) nanochannels remains unclear. In this study, AAs were modified with 0, 0.5, 1, 2, and 5wt% KH570, and C–S–H nanochannel models with grafting coverages of 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% were constructed. The KH570 modification effect was evaluated in terms of grafting characteristics, surface wettability, and water absorption, combined with molecular dynamics simulations to reveal the water transport behavior. The results indicate that KH570 was grafted onto AA surfaces, and the grafting amount increased with the concentration. The KH570 modification increased the apparent contact angle from 30.6° to 71.4° and reduced both the 24h water absorption and capillary water absorption coefficient. As the grafting coverage increased from 0% to 100%, the water filling rate decreased from 100% to 17.7%, the number of water molecules decreased from 2634 to 713, and the apparent diffusion coefficient decreased from 5.499 to 0.645 Å²/ps. Above 75% grafting coverage, the inhibitory effect on water transport approached saturation. Mechanistically, KH570 grafting inhibits water intrusion and migration by occupying hydrophilic sites, weakening hydrogen bonding interactions, and compressing the available transport space. This study defines the effective range of KH570 grafting coverage for water transport, providing a molecular-scale basis for achieving low water absorption in AAs and optimizing modifier dosage.

EcoSense: An Autonomous Polarization-Insensitive Wireless-Powered Battery-Free IoT Beacon for Live Environmental Sensing
items.venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
items.abstract: The battery-free wireless sensor beacons (WSB) are essential for realizing a green and self-sustainable operation for power-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) applications. With increasing communication activities and availability, the radio-frequency (RF) energy harvesting using a rectenna has become a reliable solution to energize the WSB wirelessly. Prior literary works indicate that the energy harvesting of a rectenna depends on the wave polarization between the rectenna and the transmitter to effectively capture the maximum incoming waves from any orientation, allowing the deployment of IoT nodes without requiring specific alignment. However, simultaneous effective energy harvesting and data transfer over a long distance at ultra-low-power is still an issue. Therefore, a novel RF-powered battery-free IoT beacon with a polarizationinsensitive (PoI) feature is developed and demonstrated for ultra-low- power IoT sensing applications. This WSB is completely integrated and miniaturized with implementing both wireless power and data transfer, which is developed on a multilayer PCB (printed circuit board). The WSB consists of a rectenna array operating at 5.2 GHz for wireless power, an integrated circuitry of a power management unit (PMU), and a Bluetooth low energy (BLE) module for data transfer. The WSB operates at a minimum received microwave power of −15.18 dBm. The results demonstrate the system to be wirelessly energized at a transfer range of 11 m away from the transmitter emitting 47.22 dBm power and realizing battery-free operation for IoT sensors. Thus, this design is suitable for orientation-independent WSB operations in IoT applications such as environmental monitoring and smart agriculture applications in remote areas.

items.title: EHAFR: An Energy Harvesting Adaptive Fuzzy Routing Framework for Prolonging the Lifetime of Wireless Sensor Networks
items.abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) have emerged as the key technological tool for environmental monitoring, agricultural applications, industrial automation, and IoT applications. However, low capacity of batteries in sensor nodes, non-uniform energy consumption, suboptimal cluster head selection strategy and high level of communication cost are among the main factors that affect the network lifetime and decrease the performance of the routing algorithm. The most popular clustering and routing protocols use a small amount of decision criteria which cause non-uniform energy dissipation, continuous reorganization of clusters and increase packet sending costs. In order to solve mentioned problems, the EHAFR system (Energy Harvesting Adaptive Fuzzy Routing) is proposed in this paper. This framework combines intelligent selection of Cluster Heads, energy aware routing and data compression strategy. First, random deployment of sensor nodes takes place and then energy aware routing discovery creates reliable communication paths among Cluster Members (CMs), Cluster Heads (CHs) and the sink node. Mamdani Fuzzy Inference System (FIS) is used in order to choose the optimal CHs according to residual energy, energy harvest, node degree, between's centrality and sink distance criteria. Additionally, Adaptive UDQ Arithmetic Coding method is used in order to compress the sensed data before its transmission. The simulation results show that the proposed EHAFR technique performs better than the other existing techniques such as CPO, DBO, and ESBOA. In general, the proposed technique has proven to be a viable and energy-efficient routing method that improves communication efficiency and extends the lifetime of the WSNs.

items.title: Dynamic remodeling of mitochondrial fission and fusion orchestrates macrophage polarization and epithelial–mesenchymal transition in silicosis
items.abstract: Accumulating evidence indicates that macrophage polarization plays a pivotal role in silicosis progression. However, whether mitochondrial fission and fusion homeostasis orchestrates alveolar macrophage polarization and subsequent epithelial-mesenchymal transition remains unclear. To delineate the role of mitochondrial dynamics in silicosis, a rat model was established by intratracheal instillation of silica particles. Histopathological alterations, cytokine profiles, and the expression of Drp1 and Mfn1/2 were evaluated at 3, 7, 14, 28, and 56 days post-exposure. Macrophage polarization was characterized by western blotting and flow cytometry. In vitro, NR8383 rat alveolar macrophages were challenged with silica and treated with Mdivi-1 (fission inhibitor) or MG-132 (proteasome inhibitor that stabilizes Mfn1/2). Polarization (iNOS/Arg1) was assessed in monoculture, whereas EMT markers (E-cadherin, vimentin) were evaluated in transwell co-culture. In vivo, silicosis progression showed an early M1/Drp1-high phase (days 3-14) shifting to a late M2/Mfn1/2-high fibrotic phase (days 28-56). Mdivi-1 blunted M1 and rescued M2; MG-132 likewise curtailed M1 and reinforced M2. Pharmacological inhibition of mitochondrial fission attenuated silica-induced EMT in vitro, restoring E-cadherin and reducing vimentin. These findings identify mitochondrial dynamics as a key regulator of the inflammation–fibrosis cascade in silicosis

items.title: Diagnosing Coordination Failure in Multiproduct Supply Chains: An Active-dual Convex-Hull Approach
items.abstract: Wholesale pricing is widely used in decentralized supply chains, and it is well known in the single-product settings that it often fails to achieve coordination. Our aim here is to study a multiproduct supply chain, not to obtain coordinating contracts, but to identify the marginal correction to the wholesale-price vector that a coordinating mechanism would need to provide. We begin with a wholesale-price Stackelberg supply chain and develop a diagnostic test for whether the induced downstream order is compatible with the integrated supply-chain optimum. The main result shows that coordination requires the wholesale-price signal to match the relevant system marginal value at the induced order vector. For manufacturer recourse models with a linear-programming structure, this condition becomes a convex-hull test over active dual slopes, representing marginal operational values from active production, capacity, and recourse constraints. When the test fails, projection onto the active hull yields a near-coordination metric and a residual identifying the required marginal contract correction. An active-set procedure generates the needed active slopes without full enumeration. Positive residual components suggest rebates, revenue sharing, buybacks, or volume discounts, whereas negative components suggest capacity-contingent charges or higher variable prices. The framework therefore translates coordination failure into a directional contract-design signal.

Описана интеграция систем управления питанием с алгоритмами MPPT, гибких наноструктурированных суперконденсаторов и сверхмалопотребляющих пассивных каналов связи (NFC, RF Backscatter). Рассмотрены аспекты применения углеродных наноматериалов и технологий Edge AI. Предложенный подход формирует методологическую основу для создания необслуживаемых медицинских патч-систем непрерывного телемедицинского мониторинга.

items.title: Deep p-Nitrophenol Removal Enabled by Self-Powered Triple-Coupling Synergy in Bio-Electro-Fenton System
items.abstract: As a refractory pollutant, p-nitrophenol (PNP) poses serious ecological risks, yet conventional remediation suffers from high energy cost and weak stability. To overcome these limitations, a triple-coupling synergistic bio-electrochemical Fenton (TS-BEF) system was engineered using a bifunctional FeCo-NC/PPy composite electrode for self-powered PNP degradation. Relying on a triple synergy-intrinsic Fe/Co bimetallic effect, interfacial FeCo-NC/PPy optimizing pyrrolic N and M-Nx site densities, and systemic synergy from applying the same material to both electrodes-the system precisely synchronizes enhanced extracellular electron transfer (EET) and the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e- ORR). This synchronization drives both bioanodic oxidation and cathodic Fenton reactions without external energy input. The TS-BEF achieved a peak power density of 2546.91 mW m-2, a 24 h cumulative H2O2 yield of 5.4 mg L-1, and 99.04% PNP degradation within 540 min, retaining 80.19% efficiency after five cycles. High-throughput analysis revealed that the anode enriched Geobacter (32.74%) and recruited Arcobacter (from 0.28% to 9.80%). The synergistic community is proposed to improve metabolic potential and establish direct and indirect EET networks. DFT calculations identified electrophilic denitration and ortho-electrophilic addition as the dominant degradation pathways. The complete operating mechanism was systematically elucidated. Overall, this self-powered technology provides an efficient, stable paradigm for refractory wastewater remediation.

items.title: Cross-Sensor Super-Resolution for Dense Spatiotemporal Reconstruction of SAR Backscatter from SMAP and Sentinel-1
items.abstract: Microwave remote sensing is central to monitoring land-surface processes such as soil moisture dynamics and freeze-thaw transitions, yet current satellite observations remain constrained by a persistent trade-off between spatial and temporal resolution. Passive microwave radiometers provide dense temporal sampling but coarse spatial detail, whereas SAR observations resolve fine spatial structure but are temporally sparse. Here, we investigate whether passive microwave brightness temperature observations can be used to reconstruct dense, sub-kilometer SAR-like backscatter time series as a cross-sensor super-resolution problem. We develop and evaluate a cross-sensor reconstruction framework that combines SMAP L-band brightness temperature with ancillary land-cover and topographic information to predict Sentinel-1 C-band backscatter over a permafrost landscape in northern Quebec, Canada. The approach reconstructs daily backscatter estimates at 556 m resolution from 9 km SMAP observations, corresponding to a 1:16 cross-sensor spatial enhancement. Evaluation across multiple years, seasons, and land-cover types shows that the reconstructed fields preserve both spatial backscatter patterns and temporal dynamics, as indicated by spatial accuracy metrics relative to Sentinel-1 observations and by temporal consistency analyses against the SMAP time series. By constraining the target resolution to a scale supported by the information content of the radiometer observations, the method avoids treating super-resolution as purely generative image synthesis and instead frames it as physically informed cross-sensor reconstruction. These results demonstrate a feasible pathway for enhancing the spatiotemporal availability of microwave observations and support future applications in soil moisture monitoring, freeze-thaw retrieval, and environmental time-series analysis in high-latitude regions.

items.title: Climate Policy Uncertainty and Clean Energy Markets in China
items.abstract: The relationship between China’s clean energy markets and China’s climate policy uncertainty (CCPU) has generally been considered weak in the literature. We challenge this view by examining the degree and structure of dependence between CCPU and the returns of six clean energy sub-industry indices, including solar, nuclear, wind, new energy vehicles, fuel cell, and smart grid, over the period 2010-2025. Using a quantile regression approach, we find that although mean-based models indicate a weak relationship, the CCPU-return dependence does exist but varies across the distribution. In particular, the dependence is more pronounced in the middle to upper quantiles (50%-90%). At the sector level, the solar industry is the only sector to display a negative dependence with CCPU in the lower tail of the return distribution (25%), while such a relationship is pervasive in higher tails across the sectors. Our subperiod analysis shows that the dependence between CCPU and clean energy returns is time-varying. The Paris Agreement period (2016-2019) exhibits a higher degree of dependence and a stronger dependence structure in most sectors, whereas the COVID-19 period (2020-2021) is characterized by stronger short-term co-movement but less stable patterns. Our findings provide new evidence that the relationship between CCPU and clean energy sub-industry returns is heterogeneous across quantiles, sectors, and event periods, with important implications for portfolio diversification, risk management, and climate-related financial policy.​

items.title: Ambient backscatter communications in cellular systems
items.abstract: The emergence of battery-free energy-harvesting devices within next-generation cellular networks has motivated the concept of Ambient Internet of Things (A-IoT), aiming to enable ultra-lowcomplexity maintenance-free massive deployments. Ambient backscatter communication (AmBC) is a key enabler of this vision, as it allows devices to transmit information by modulating and reflecting existing radio frequency (RF) signals without generating active RF carriers. However, integrating AmBC into cellular systems presents significant challenges, including severe directpath interference (DPI), weak scattered signal power, time-varying fading channels, and the need to operate without additional spectrum or infrastructure. This thesis presents a comprehensive investigation of cellular-integrated AmBC, focusing on seamless coexistence with Long Term Evolution (LTE) and New Radio (NR) systems. The central idea is to parasitically reuse continuously transmitted cellular pilot and data signals for both energy harvesting and communication, thereby eliminating the need for dedicated carriers, hardware modifications, or additional spectrum allocation. By interpreting the backscatter device (BD) as a secondary system that modulates the effective channel response, the proposed framework detects BD information through variations in channel state information estimated at the primary receiver. To address the low signal-to-noise ratio caused by DPI, this work introduces a frequency-shift keying (FSK)-based AmBC scheme that shifts backscattered signals into the Doppler domain, effectively separating them from the dominant direct path. Closed-form detection criteria and probability expressions are derived, and bit error rate (BER) performance is analytically characterized. Furthermore, a coherent receiver architecture synchronized by primary cellular pilots is developed, enabling reliable BD detection without additional training overhead. To mitigate channel dynamics and further enhance detection robustness, a data-assisted channel-estimation approach is proposed. By iteratively incorporating decoded primary data symbols into this channel estimation process, the receiver significantly improves estimation accuracy and BD detection performance. The feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed methods are validated through theoretical analysis, link-level simulations, and extensive over-theair experiments using a real-world prototype. The results establish a unified analytical–numerical–experimental framework for cellular AmBC and demonstrate its capability to achieve reliable, ultra-low-power communication suitable for large-scale A-IoT deployments. This work provides both theoretical foundations and practical design guidelines for integrating ambient backscatter into future 6G cellular networks, advancing sustainable and energy-autonomous Internet of Things communications.

items.title: Advanced Antenna Technologies for Communication, IoT and Medical Applications

items.abstract: This book presents innovations in advanced antenna technologies, including advanced wearable antennas, energy-harvesting antennas, and modules. Moreover, the book presents Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces, Inverted Microstrip Line Phase Shifter Technique for Antennas, and Enhancing wireless performance with Antenna distance-based modulation. Wearable technology provides a powerful new tool to medical services, surgical rehabilitation services, sports training, and IOT systems. Wireless Body Area Networks, WBANs, can record electrocardiograms, measure body temperature and blood pressure, measure heartbeat rate, arterial blood pressure, electro-dermal activity, and other healthcare parameters. Wearable devices will be an important part of individuals’ daily lives in the next decade. Wearable technology typically includes communication capabilities, enabling users to access information in real time. Several wireless technologies are used to handle data collection and processing by medical systems. The collected data may be stored or transmitted to a medical center for analysis. Wearable devices gather raw data, which is fed to a database or to a software application for analysis. This analysis may result in a response that alerts a physician to contact a patient experiencing abnormal symptoms. Wearable technology may offer scanning and sensing features that mobile phones and laptop computers do not. The book may be a valuable resource for antenna designers, academic researchers, communication engineers, and communication systems project managers involved in the development and manufacturing of antenna networks and communication systems. The information presented aims to inspire further innovation and application in this field.

items.title: A comparative and critical study of EEGNet for fNIRS-driven cognitive load classification
items.abstract: Accurately classifying cognitive load from functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) signals remains a significant challenge due to temporal variability, inter-subject differences, and sensitivity to preprocessing choices. This study provides a comprehensive evaluation of EEGNet for fNIRS-based cognitive load classification by systematically examining the effects of temporal segmentation strategies (overlapping vs. non-overlapping), window lengths (10s, 20s, 30s), feature extraction methods (Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Fast Independent Component Analysis (FastICA)), learning rate configurations (fixed and adaptive), and evaluation protocols (random split vs. subject-independent (SI)). Results from random-split experiments show that overlapping segmentation, combined with smaller fixed learning rates (0.01-0.001), yields the highest accuracies, due to temporal redundancy and dense sampling of hemodynamic transitions. However, SI evaluation reveals a substantial drop in accuracy, demonstrating limited generalization to unseen participants. Under SI evaluation, non-overlapping segmentation outperformed overlapping windows, with the best accuracy of 56.11% achieved using PCA features with a 20-second window and a 0.1 learning rate. These findings indicate that eliminating temporal redundancy helps the model learn more robust and generalizable representations of cognitive load across individuals. Although adaptive learning rate strategy improved training stability, it did not surpass the performance of optimally selected fixed learning rates. The study highlights the critical role of segmentation strategy and learning rate selection in improving model generalization and identifies methodological considerations essential for developing reliable, real-time, and SI cognitive load classification systems using fNIRS.

items.title: A Space-Spatial frequency Mutual Coherence Design Framework for Interferometric Wafer Nanotopography
items.abstract: Wafer nanotopography is a key surface-quality metric in advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Its measurement over the spatial-frequency band of 0.05-5 mm-1 relies on an interferometer with low coherent noise and adequate response to small-amplitude surface-height errors. However, conventional interferometer design lacks a quantitative link between illumination spatial coherence and band-specific measurement performance. Here, we establish a Space–Spatial-Frequency Mutual Coherence Transfer Model for partially coherent interferometry and introduce band-limited equivalent height noise (BLEHN) as an optimization metric integrating coherent noise, interferometric transfer, and fringe contrast over the target band. For a 100-mm-aperture Fizeau interferometer, the framework identifies an effective source-diameter near 0.58 mm. We constructed a 4-in. wafer nanotopography interferometer for experimental validation, using a 0.5-mm extended source, the background RMS noise is reduced from 5.03 to 0.93 nm (81.5%), and the minimum resolvable period from 0.38 to 0.15 mm (60.5%). Full-aperture wafer measurements yield a mean Dev99.95 of 67.58 nm with a standard deviation of 0.45 nm over 15 repeated measurements. These results validate the proposed Space–Spatial-Frequency Mutual Coherence design framework and demonstrate quantitative spatial-coherence optimization for balancing coherent-noise suppression and band-specific surface-height response in wafer nanotopography interferometry. To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first to establish a unified spatial–spatial-frequency mutual-coherence description for interferometric measurement and apply it to quantitative interferometer design for wafer nanotopography measurement.

A Self-starting Boost Converter with Multi-Mode Operation and Direct-Sensing MPPT for Photovoltaic Energy Harvesting
items.abstract: This paper presents a self-starting boost converter designed for photovoltaic energy harvesting. Multi-mode operation accelerates circuit startup, allowing the interface to efficiently reach its operating voltage within a very short time. A direct-sensing maximum power point tracking (MPPT) technique is introduced to improve power conversion efficiency across a wide illumination range. In addition, a periodic sleep mode is incorporated to reduce overall power consumption while maintaining high MPPT tracking accuracy. Fabricated in a 180 nm CMOS process, the proposed circuit achieves self-startup within 72.8 ms at an input voltage of 180 mV, with a peak tracking efficiency of 99.6% and an end-to-end efficiency of 90.6%. Compared to state-of-the-art designs, the proposed solution offers a better balance between power consumption and tracking performance.

items.title: A Ropeway-Integrated Obstruction Awareness System (RIOAS): Auxiliary Marker-Cable Architecture, Photometric and Radio-Beacon Coverage Modeling, and Structural Load Analysis for Aerial-Cableway Aircraft-Collision-Hazard Mitigation
items.abstract: Aerial ropeway installations (cable cars, gondola lifts, and aerial tramways) present a thin, high-tension, skyline hazard to low-ying aircraft and helicopters that has been implicated in at least one catastrophic loss-of-life event caused by an aircraft severing a ropeway track cable. Current obstruction-marking practice, codied in ICAO Annex 14 Chapter 6, relies primarily on passive spherical markers clamped directly onto the load-bearing haul or track cable; such markers add mass and aerodynamic drag to a safety-critical structural member, oer negligible night-time conspicuity unless separately illuminated, and provide no cockpit alerting channel independent of the pilot's visual scan. This paper develops and computationally evaluates a Ropeway-Integrated Obstruction Awareness System (RIOAS): a dedicated, mechanically independent auxiliary messenger cable strung parallel to the primary ropeway cable(s) on load-rated tower cross-arms, carrying actively powered photometric beacons and coded visual placards, combined with a station-mounted VHF/UHF advisory radio beacon. We formulate a parabolic-catenary structural load model (self-weight, radial ice accretion, and quasi-static wind drag) for the auxiliary cable and its tower reactions; a photometric detection-range model based on Allard's Law and Koschmieder atmospheric transmissivity; a standard 4/3-Earth-radius radio-line-of-sight coverage model for the station beacon; and a kinematic screening model that compares the resulting detection range against the FAA's documented 12.5-second average pilot see-identify-decide-respond interval for a range of aircraft closing speeds. All models are implemented in open, unit-tested Python and exercised through Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation (20 000 samples) and a Saltelli-sampled, Jansen-estimated variance-based (Sobol) global sensitivity analysis. Under representative alpine design loads, the auxiliary cable adds 3.35 kN of vertical reaction per intermediate tower and achieves a computed night-time detection range of approximately 13.4 km (versus 0 km for an unlit passive marker ball and 5.6 km for a retrotted low-intensity obstruction light, under identical 10 km meteorological visibility) while, by construction, transmitting zero additional load to the primary haul cable. The kinematic screening analysis shows the proposed system provides an adequate warning margin under the FAA reaction-time criterion for all rotary-wing and general-aviation closing speeds considered (≤ 200 kn) but is, by the same criterion, computationally inadequate in daytime lighting conditions for xed-wing transits above approximately 250300 kn a regime that includes the closing speed of the aircraft involved in the 1998 Cavalese cable-car accident. This closing-speed threshold is reported as an explicit, falsiable boundary of the system's claimed eectiveness rather than as a universally applicable guarantee. The work is a conceptual, computational engineering study: no physical prototype has been built or eld-tested, and all quantitative outputs are reproducible from the enclosed code and are traceable to either rst-principles physics, cited standards, or explicitly labeled parametric design assumptions.

items.title: A Hardware-isolated, Sub-Millisecond Runtime Audit Architecture for Autonomous Multi-agent Systems via Pre-actuation State Dissolution
items.abstract: Autonomous multi-agent systems now commit consequential financial and physical actions on timescales that exclude human supervision. The interval between an unaligned intention forming in a model's residual stream and its serialization into an external API call is on the order of 200 ms; the interval between an anomaly surfacing and a human operator orienting to it is on the order of 200 s. Every deployed safety mechanism perimeter allows lists, API rate limits, output classifiers, human-in-the-loop gates is positioned on the wrong side of that three-order-ofmagnitude asymmetry, and each fails structurally rather than incidentally: they enumerate actions against an adversary that generates compositions. We present the Automated Metacognitive Protocol (AMP), a runtime audit architecture that relocates enforcement from the action boundary into the inference path. AMP installs non-differentiable shadow taps on the residual stream at selected layers, projects hidden states through low-rank audit operators into a permission manifold expressed in the model's own representational geometry, and scores divergence by Mahalanobis distance under Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage covariance estimation. Dualpath temporal filtering, exponentially weighted moving average for acute divergence, one-sided CUSUM for sub-threshold drift triggers pre-actuation state dissolution: orthogonal projection of the identified unaligned direction out of the residual stream, recursively validated across the remaining stack until intent magnitude falls below a zero-weight vacancy threshold. We derive an analytical latency budget of approximately 6.6 MFLOP per token across twelve tapped layers at d=8192, k=32, corresponding to under 20 µs end-to-end on dedicated silicon against a 200 ms action boundary. We formalize three topological failure modes of goal-directed optimizers as a computable aberration risk vector, prove that local action predicates cannot bound non-separable exposure functionals, and specify hardware isolation and zero-power fail-safe conditions under which the resulting governance floor is invariant to counterparty intelligence. The architecture is presented as a specification with analytical guarantees; empirical validation is stated as required future work.

items.title: A Comprehensive Review of Battery‐Free Energy Efficient RF and Microwave Systems
items.abstract: Battery‐free radiofrequency (RF) and microwave systems have emerged as a promising solution for enabling long‐lifetime, maintenance‐free wireless sensing and communication platforms by eliminating conventional battery dependence. These systems operate by harvesting ambient or dedicated electromagnetic energy, converting it to usable electrical power, and utilizing ultralow‐power circuit and communication techniques to sustain sensing, processing, and wireless data transmission. This paper presents a comprehensive review of battery‐free energy‐efficient RF and microwave systems, covering the evolution of the field, energy harvesting and rectenna modeling techniques, power management strategies, ultralow‐power communication methods, and energy‐aware networking protocols. The review further examines key enabling circuit technologies, including subthreshold microwave integrated circuits, passive and backscatter‐based transmitters, and envelope‐detection receivers designed for nanowatt‐to‐microwatt operation. Recent experimental developments in battery‐free Internet of Things (IoT) nodes, wearable and implantable platforms, and smart‐environment monitoring systems are analyzed to highlight the transition from laboratory prototypes to real‐world deployments. Performance evaluation metrics such as RF‐to‐DC conversion efficiency, communication reliability, scalability, and system lifetime are discussed using representative experimental results from recent literature. The paper also identifies major open challenges, including energy intermittency, miniaturization constraints, and security considerations, and outlines future research directions such as integration with 5G/6G infrastructure, AI‐assisted energy management, and advanced materials for flexible and multiband harvesting structures. The review demonstrates that advances in rectenna codesign, ultralow‐power circuit architectures, adaptive communication techniques, and network‐level coordination are rapidly enabling practical battery‐free wireless systems, positioning RF and microwave energy harvesting as a key technology for sustainable massive IoT and long‐term autonomous sensing applications.

A 4096-element 3D-integrated Si-SiN optical phased array for high-power coherent LiDAR
items.abstract: Integrated optical phased arrays (OPAs) are pivotal for next-generation solid-state light detection and ranging (LiDAR), offering high-speed, inertia-free beam steering in a compact form factor. However, achieving high angular resolution alongside multi-watt emission power remains a formidable challenge. In this work, we present a 3D-integrated silicon-silicon nitride (Si-SiN) hybrid OPA comprising 4096 (4 × 1024) elements, packaged with a CMOS driver chip via flip-chip bonding. The proposed heterogeneous Si-SiN architecture leverages PN carrier-depletion phase shifting with sub-nanosecond response capability, currently demonstrating a 2 μs CMOS-driven beam switching time and ultra-low-power (1.5 μW/π), while delivering an angular resolution of 0.038° × 0.017° (FWHM) and a total main-lobe CW emission power of 1.5 W at a 20 W high-power injection. This approach effectively circumvents silicon's nonlinear limitations while maintaining high-density integration. System-level validations include indoor coherent detection and a four-channel phase-locked synthetic aperture scheme that successfully compresses the beam divergence to 300 μrad. This architecture provides a scalable roadmap for the development of high-performance, long-range solid-state LiDAR systems.

items.title: Wideband millimeter-wave antenna design with hammer-shaped slot and enhanced radiation characteristics
items.venue: Intellectual Journal of Energy Harvesting and Storage
items.abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a novel hammer-shaped slotted microstrip patch antenna optimized for operation at 27 GHz. The proposed antenna structure features a truncated ground plane and is tailored to support wideband applications in the millimeter-wave (mmWave) frequency spectrum. Key performance parameters such as return loss (S11), voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR), far-field radiation characteristics, and gain are thoroughly analyzed. Simulation results show that the antenna achieves a wide operating bandwidth from 24.5 GHz to 30.9 GHz, with a peak gain of 6.35 dB and an excellent return loss of −37.8 dB at the central frequency. These promising results suggest that the antenna is well-suited for high-frequency applications such as 5G and radar systems.

items.title: Polarization-Shift Backscatter Identification for SWIPT-Based Battery-Free Sensor Nodes
items.abstract: Battery-Free Sensor Nodes (BFSNs) used in Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT) systems often rely on lightweight communication protocols with minimal security overhead due to strict energy constraints. As a result, conventional protocol-dependent security mechanisms cannot be employed, leaving BFSNs vulnerable to replay, spoofing, and other security threats. This paper explores a protocol-independent security mechanism that enhances BFSN security by exploiting the power wave for controlled backscattering. The method introduces a Manchester-encoded digital private key generated by the BFSN’s low-power microcontroller and backscattered through a polarization-shifting module enabled by a fail-safe RF switch, thereby avoiding the need for a dedicated backscattering rectifier. A LoRaWAN-based BFSN integrating this add-on module was implemented to experimentally validate the approach. Results show successful extraction of the backscattered key with minimal energy overhead (approximately 95 µJ for a 3 ms identification sequence), while the original high-efficiency RF rectifier used for harvesting remains unmodified. The orthogonal polarization between the incoming and backscattered waves additionally reduces clutter and cross-jamming effects. These findings demonstrate that secure identification can be seamlessly incorporated into existing BFSNs without altering their core architecture, offering an easy-to-integrate and energy-efficient solution for improving security in SWIPT-based sensing systems.

items.title: EsTRACE—Es-Layer TRAnsient Cloud Explorer: PlanarSat Mission Concept and Early-Phase Design (Bid, CoDR, PDR) for Sporadic-E Sensing
items.abstract: Sporadic-E (Es) layers can strongly perturb HF/VHF propagation and create intermittent interference, motivating higher-revisit monitoring at the frequencies most affected. EsTRACE (Es-layer TRAnsient Cloud Explorer) is a PlanarSat mission concept that transmits sequential beacons in the 28/50 MHz amateur bands using FT4 (weak-signal digital) and CW (continuous wave) waveforms and leverages distributed amateur receiver networks for near-real-time SNR mapping. This paper documents the early-phase spacecraft design from the Bid/proposal phase (Bid), through the Conceptual Design Review (CoDR), to the Preliminary Design Review (PDR), using a power-first sizing loop that couples link-budget closure to duty cycle and solar-array area under a free-tumbling, batteryless constraint. The analysis supports conceptual feasibility of the architecture under stated antenna and ground-segment assumptions; on-orbit demonstration and measured RF/antenna characterization are identified as required future validation steps.

items.title: Tulip tree leaf-shaped microstrip MIMO antenna utilizing the superformula
items.venue: Journal of King Saud University - Science
items.abstract: This paper introduces an innovative design for a microstrip patch antenna (MPA) that is inspired by the geometry of a tulip tree leaf. The design implements the Superformula methodology, as established by Gielis. The proposed antenna operates at frequencies of 5.2 GHz and 10.1 GHz, achieving a notable impedance bandwidth with a compact physical size of λ/5.18 x λ/5.18 at the resonance frequency. The leaf-shaped patch antenna demonstrates several benefits, including enhanced return loss and a reduced footprint when compared to traditional MPAs, thereby indicating its substantial potential for applications in wireless systems. The proposed design facilitates the integration of two identical antennas in close proximity to achieve a Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) configuration. This advancement is expected to enhance both system capacity and link reliability. This research contributes significant insights into the advancement of efficient antenna systems that are suitable for contemporary communication technologies.

items.title: Smart Textiles: An Interdisciplinary Overview of Advances, Applications, and Future Prospects
items.abstract: Smart textiles represent an innovative integration of nanotechnology, materials science, and wearable electronics, offering capabilities far beyond those of traditional textiles. This thorough review covers recent advances in engineered nanomaterial-based textiles, particularly discussing groundbreaking applications of these materials in health, energy, military, and consumer sectors. All four categories are critically reviewed: (1) Protective textiles incorporating flame-resistant nanocoatings, antibacterial nanoparticles, and UV-blocking semiconductor nanoparticles; (2) Energy-harvesting technologies based on piezoelectric, triboelectric, and thermoelectric nanomaterials, specifically designed for self-powered electronics; (3) Physiological monitoring interfaces using graphene sensors and optical fibers, intended for real-time biomedical monitoring and tracking; (4) Active materials exhibiting color-changing, shape-memory, and thermally responsive properties. The review highlights advances in materials science, including MXene-based textiles for electromagnetic shielding, phase-change materials for dynamic thermal control, and plasmonic nanostructures for interactive displays. We also discuss scalable processing technologies, including electrospinning of conductive polymers, roll-to-roll fabrication of textile-based solar cells, and atomic layer deposition of nanocomposite thin films. The emerging themes of biocompatibility in electronics, AI-based adaptive technologies, and sustainable nanotextiles are key research and development areas for next-generation textiles. By synthesizing evidence from more than 230 studies, this review provides researchers and industry stakeholders with insight into current capabilities and future opportunities for integrating smart textiles into practical applications.

items.title: From Exposure to Response: Mechanisms of Plant Interaction with Electromagnetic Fields Used in Smart Agriculture
items.abstract: Smart agriculture technology is rapidly spreading for its economic benefits and increase in farming efficiency. The management of agricultural activities is fulfilled by a network of connected devices and sensors, using wireless technologies and software to exchange data over the Internet. The electromagnetic fields (EMFs) these systems use increase the background level in farmlands, and the crop plants are exposed to unusual levels of unnatural, polarized, coherent, and variable EM radiation. This combination determines EMF influence on plants. Many studies found effects at different levels of organization—molecular, organismal, and even ecosystem levels—but the underlying mechanisms are still not well understood. In this review paper, we attempted to clarify possible mechanisms on the very basic molecular level involved in the realization of biological effects, discussing the interaction of EMFs with water molecules in living systems, from their effects on biologically significant molecules, membranes, ion channels, and ion transport, oxidative processes in cells, and photosynthesis to the effects on plant growth and development. In conclusion, we discuss the obstacles to defining the conditions for the manifestation of beneficial or adverse effects and setting exposure limits.

items.title: Energy Harvesting Techniques Enabling Self-Powered IoT Devices
items.venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
items.abstract: The swift expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) has heightened the difficulty of supplying power to billions of distributed, low-energy devices. Traditional batteries impose restrictions on longevity, scalability, and sustainability. Energy harvesting (EH) facilitates self-powered or energy-autonomous IoT nodes by transforming ambient energy—mechanical, solar, wind, thermal, radio-frequency (RF), and sound—into electrical energy. This concise review outlines the fundamental EH mechanisms, architectures, transducers, power management techniques, storage solutions, and security issues pertinent to IoT. The focus is on practical trade-offs, market readiness, and prospective research avenues aimed at achieving sustainable and secure IoT and Internet of Nano-Things (IoNT) systems.

items.title: A Review on Near-Field and Far-Field Wireless Power Transfer Technologies
items.abstract: Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) technologies are rapidly maturing, offering alternatives to traditional wired connections in applications ranging from consumer electronics to industrial automation. This review provides a technical analysis of WPT methodologies published between 2010 and 2025, explicitly distinguishing between non-radiative near-field techniques (specifically Inductive Power Transfer [IPT] and Capacitive Power Transfer [CPT]) and radiative far-field systems (Microwave Power Transfer [MPT] and Laser Power Transfer [LPT]). Unlike previous reviews that categorize primarily by coupling mechanism, this paper proposes a novel multi-parametric classification framework incorporating efficiency, alignment sensitivity, and emerging operational paradigms such as AI-optimized tuning and acoustic transfer. The analysis evaluates the engineering trade-offs between short-range, high-efficiency inductive systems and long-range, lower-efficiency radiative links. Furthermore, the paper identifies critical technical barriers to commercialization, specifically focusing on electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), biological safety (SAR) limits, and end-to-end system efficiency. Finally, the review extends beyond the physics to provide a rigorous economic analysis of the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) for electric vehicle infrastructure and industrial IoT, highlighting the strategic viability of WPT in future smart grids.
